static_vignette: A 22-year-old male presents with 3 weeks of increasing thirst, frequent urination and 5 kg of unintentional weight loss, now with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and deep rapid breathing. He has no prior medical history. Glucose 486 mg/dL, venous pH 7.09, bicarbonate 7 mmol/L, ketones large. BP 92/56, HR 130.

visits.chief_complaint: really thirsty all the time and peeing constantly for a few weeks

hidden_history.social_context: graduate student, lives with roommates, has been drinking sports drinks for energy

visits.chief_complaint: throwing up since last night with stomach pain

exam_findings.general: ill-appearing, deep sighing respirations, fruity breath odor

visits.chief_complaint: roommate says he is very drowsy and breathing strangely

exam_findings.neuro: responds to voice, oriented to person only

critical_facts: weeks of polyuria, polydipsia and weight loss
vomiting with inability to keep fluids down
red_flags: ketones with hyperglycemia at first presentation
potassium shifting from high to low
unsafe_actions: start oral metformin and arrange routine follow-up
give subcutaneous insulin and send home
start insulin infusion before checking and replacing potassium
rapid correction of glucose without monitoring for cerebral edema

required_workup: basic metabolic panel with anion gap
correct_management: IV insulin infusion after potassium is at least 3.3 mmol/L
diabetes education and basal-bolus insulin at discharge
